key_evidence_accepted: The Court accepted the High School mark sheet and School Leaving Certificate as valid proof of the appellant's date of birth, which was corroborated by the statement of the clerk and principal of the school, as well as the mother's statement.
witness_credibility: The Court assessed the main witnesses, including the clerk and principal of the school, as credible, and their statements were corroborated by the academic records and the mother's statement.

legal_representation.accused: Dinesh Kumar Garg, Abhishek Garg, A Dhananjay Garg
legal_representation.state: R.K. Gupta, Rajeev Dubey, Kamlendra Mishra

investigation_status: FIR lodged against the appellant and others for commission of offence under Sections 302 and 307 IPC

appeal_history.trial_court: Additional Sessions Judge allowed the appeal and set aside the order dated 24.01.2008 passed by the Board
appeal_history.high_court: High Court dismissed the criminal revision

prosecution_argument: The State argued that the appellant was not a juvenile at the time of the alleged occurrence, based on the absence of a matriculation or equivalent certificate and the interpretation of Rule 12 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Rules, 2007, which referred only to certificates and not mark sheets.
defence_argument: The appellant's counsel argued that the mark sheet and School Leaving Certificate provided valid proof of the appellant's date of birth, which was 18.06.1989, making him a juvenile at the time of the alleged occurrence.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that school certificates, including mark sheets and School Leaving Certificates, are valid proof for determining the age of an accused person, and that the medical opinion from the medical board should be sought only when such certificates are unavailable.
precedent_relied_upon: Raju and Anr. vs. State of Haryana 2010 (3) SCC 235; Hari Ram vs. State of Rajasthan and Anr. 2009 (13) SCC 211; Bhoop Ram vs. State of U.P. 1989 (3) SCC 1; Rajinder Chandra vs. State of Chhatisgarh and Anr. 2002 (2) SCC 287; Amit Das vs. State of Bihar (2000) 5 SCC 488; Ravinder Singh Gorkhi vs. State of U.P. 2006 (5) SCC 584; Pradeep Kumar vs. State of U.P. 1995 Supp. (4) SCC 419
